description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of different models as a function of the occurrence number of a specific event or data point. The x-axis represents the occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis measures the accuracy percentage, ranging from 65% to 80%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different model: Base, FT, MEND, MEMIT, ROME, and IKE. The Base line is marked with a solid black line and circle markers, the FT line with a solid blue line and triangle markers, the MEND line with a solid brown line and square markers, the MEMIT line with a solid purple line and diamond markers, the ROME line with a solid green line and pentagon markers, and the IKE line with a solid red line and star markers. All lines show a general upward trend, indicating that accuracy increases as the occurrence number increases. The Base line starts at approximately 70% accuracy at the lowest occurrence number and ends at around 80% at the highest occurrence number. The FT line starts at around 65% and ends at about 75%. The MEND line starts at approximately 70% and ends at around 78%. The MEMIT line starts at about 68% and ends at around 76%. The ROME line starts at around 72% and ends at about 77%. The IKE line starts at approximately 67% and ends at around 74%. The plot does not include any peaks, declines, or steady trends beyond the general upward trend observed across all lines.
